atelier.lead: Bretda is a small house on the southern coast of Brazil. We build a limited number of tables each year — each one by hand, each one signed.
atelier.c1p: It began with two cabinetmakers, one bench, and a refusal to make anything ordinary. The bench is larger now — the refusal is the same.
atelier.c2h: One block of wood. Six hundred hours.
atelier.c2p: Each table is cut from a single piece of Brazilian hardwood, joined without compromise where the eye can reach, and finished by hand until the grain reads like silk.
atelier.p1p: Proportions drawn for your room, your ceiling, your light.
atelier.p2p: A single hardwood block, selected, rested, and cut to the grain.
atelier.p3p: Assembled by hand over weeks — no shortcut where it counts.
atelier.p4p: Numbered, signed, and prepared for insured white-glove delivery.
atelier.quote: “We do not make many. We make one, completely, and then begin again.”
